title: Anthropic adds install-as-app to Claude Artifacts: AI-generated tools can be installed on macOS and Windows desktops

content_html:
Getting AI to casually “make” a small web tool in Claude is nothing new. What is new is that these creations used to live only in browser tabs, disappearing as soon as the window was closed. On November 25, Anthropic introduced an “Install as app” option for interactive Artifacts, letting users install AI-generated apps directly onto macOS and Windows desktops and launch them as standalone software.

Install creations like web apps

According to the official description, installed Artifacts apps get their own desktop toolbar icon, similar to installing a web app on your computer: no need to visit them through a browser tab every time—just click the icon to launch them. The feature is currently in Beta and is gradually rolling out to macOS and Windows desktop users. For Anthropic, this update extends Artifacts from temporary interactions inside the browser to everyday desktop use.

You decide how much permission to grant

Security boundaries are left to users to set in tiers. Under the default permission mode, the app runs like a browser tab, with behavior boundaries consistent with the web. If you want it to feel more like “real software,” you can grant additional app permissions, including sending notifications, intercepting keyboard shortcuts, and displaying above other app windows. Users with more demanding needs can go further and grant full computer access. Different permission settings change both the system features the app can use and the range of actions it can perform.

From impromptu creations in a chat window to standalone apps that live on the desktop, Claude-generated works are stepping out of the chat box.
